standard_prerequisites.name: Excellent rings are quasi-excellent and universally catenary
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives both halves of the first implication.

standard_prerequisites.name: The locality statement for universal catenarity: an affine open chart of a universally catenary scheme has universally catenary coordinate ring, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Converts universal catenarity of the scheme into universal catenarity of the relevant coordinate ring, and conversely.

standard_prerequisites.name: Quasi-excellence of a scheme means that every point has an affine open neighbourhood with quasi-excellent coordinate ring
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the chart whose coordinate ring is quasi-excellent.

core_obligations: First implication: if the scheme is excellent then it is quasi-excellent because excellent rings are quasi-excellent, and it is universally catenary because excellent rings are universally catenary, using the locality statement for universal catenarity (proof lines 3448-3453).

Second implication: given quasi-excellence and universal catenarity, at each point choose an affine open neighbourhood with quasi-excellent coordinate ring, note that the same coordinate ring is universally catenary by the locality statement applied to the universally catenary scheme, and conclude that it is excellent, which is the definition of excellence for the scheme (proof lines 3454-3459).
proof_roadmap: Use the implications between the ring-theoretic properties for one direction, and for the other combine the local definition of quasi-excellence with the locality statement for universal catenarity (proof lines 3448-3459).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that a scheme is excellent exactly when it is quasi-excellent and universally catenary (statement lines 3439-3446). The counted proof is short and complete: one direction follows from the corresponding implications for rings together with the locality of universal catenarity, and the other direction chooses at each point an affine neighbourhood with quasi-excellent coordinate ring, observes that this ring is universally catenary by the same locality statement, and concludes excellence (proof lines 3448-3459). It is H2: both directions are carried out in the counted span, with the cited input being the locality statement for universal catenarity.
